title: Can Saudi Arabia rebuild Yemen’s fractured anti-Houthi coalition?
gist: With the Strait of Hormuz blockaded, Saudi Arabia is backing a Yemeni government offensive (Operation Dawn of Yemen, launched Oct. 4) to reverse Houthi gains on the Red Sea coast and secure Bab el-Mandeb, its key energy export gateway. Riyadh is leaning on UAE-backed Yemeni factions, testing whether a shared Houthi threat can overcome rivalries that have fractured the anti-Houthi camp and strained Saudi-Emirati ties.

themes.theme: Bab el-Mandeb as Saudi export lifeline

insights.claim: With the Strait of Hormuz blockaded, the Bab el-Mandeb Strait has become a vital gateway for Saudi energy exports, and securing it is Saudi Arabia's immediate objective in Yemen.
insights.speaker: Francesco Schiavi
insights.so_what: Houthi control or disruption near Bab el-Mandeb would threaten the main remaining outlet for Saudi crude while Hormuz is shut, a major oil supply risk.
insights.quote: Saudi Arabia's immediate objective is to reverse Houthi gains along the Red Sea coast and secure the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, a vital gateway for Saudi energy exports as the Strait of Hormuz remains blockaded.
